subject: Basic Mechanical Engineering

questions.markdown:
Superheated steam at 10 bar is taken out from a boiler and is passed through a supply pipeline to a nearby industry for its use. The industry strictly requires only wet steam with a dryness fraction of 0.8. (i) If the heat loss through the supply pipeline is 500 kJ/kg, what is the temperature of superheated steam at the boiler exit? (ii) If the heat loss in the supply pipeline is limited to 30% of latent heat of vaporization, what should be the condition of steam at boiler exit in order to ensure that the steam supplied to the industry has the required dryness fraction of 0.8? (iii) If the thermal insulation on the supply pipeline is such that the steam does not loose any heat as it passes through the supply pipeline, should the boiler still supply superheated steam? Elaborate your answer.

Assume specific heat of superheated steam as 2.25 kJ/kgK.

Two boilers supply equal quantity of steam to a common pipeline at 15 bar pressure. The steam from boiler-1 is superheated at 250$^\circ$C while the condition of steam from boiler-2 is unknown. The steam in the common pipeline is wet with a dryness fraction of 0.7 at 15 bar. (i) Determine the condition of steam supplied by boiler-2. (ii) If the steam generation rate from boiler-2 is 10 times higher than its fuel supply rate and feed water is supplied at 20$^\circ$C, what will be the efficiency of boiler-2? Assume specific heat of superheated steam and saturated water as 2.25 kJ/kgK and 4.187 kJ/kgK respectively.

The calorific value of fuel supplied to boiler-2 is 22 MJ/kg.

A belt drive transmits power between two pulleys that are placed 1.8 m apart with a velocity ratio of 0.2. The belt has an angle of contact of 4 radians with the pulley. The diameter of the larger pulley is 1 m and the driver pulley rotates at 1400 rpm. The initial tension in the belt is 0.8 kN and coefficient of friction is 0.28. Determine the power transmitted by the belt drive. Also find the length of the belt.

A compound gear train consists of six gear wheels A, B, C, D, E & F where A is the driver gear and F is the driven gear. The number of teeth on gear A and F are 90 and 20 respectively. Gear B meshes with gear A and is mounted on the same shaft with gear C which has 80 teeth. Gear D meshes with gear C and is mounted on the same shaft with gear E. Gear F meshes with gear E. The velocity ratio from gear A to F is 80. The velocity ratio from A to B is equal to the velocity ratio from C to D and E to F. Show the gearing arrangement and determine the number of teeth for gears B, D and E.

An engineer wants to transmit power using gear drives in an engineering application and is encountered with the following two constraints:

Constraint 1: The axes of the driver and driven shafts are inclined to one another and intersect when produced.

Constraint 2: The driving and driven shafts have their axes at right angles and are non-coplanar.

Name the best possible gear drive system that the engineer should choose to overcome each constraint separately and explain its characteristics with a neat sketch.

Which engine will you select if power should be developed in every revolution of engine crankshaft using petrol as fuel? Explain its operation with a neat sketch clearly showing the piston position in each stroke.

A single cylinder IC engine generates an output power of 10 kW when operating at 2000 rpm. The engine consumes 2 cc/s of petrol and has a compression ratio of 10. The engine is capable of converting 40% of combustion heat energy into power inside the cylinder during power stroke. The volume of the charge inside the cylinder at the end of compression stroke is 0.2 litre. If the engine is designed such that the power is developed for every two revolutions of crankshaft in a given cycle of operation, (i) what will be the brake torque? (ii) what is the mean effective pressure? (iii) what is the brake specific fuel consumption in kg/kWh? Assume calorific value of fuel as 22000 kJ/kg and specific gravity of fuel as 0.7 and density of water as 1000 kg/m$^3$.

Two machining operations are to be carried out on a metal rod using a lathe machine. In the first operation, the length of the rod needs to be reduced. In the second operation, a serrated surface should be generated on the rod surface. Name and explain the suitable lathe operations with a neat sketch.
Elaborate the important lathe specifications with a neat sketch.
With a neat sketch elaborate the important features of radial drilling machine.
Explain in detail the importance of machining and shrinkage allowances in casting process?

The following machining operation needs to be carried out using a drilling machine:

(i) Rightsizing of an existing hole.

(ii) Threading inside an existing hole

Name the suitable drilling operation for each case and explain its characteristics with a neat sketch.
Explain with a neat sketch the principle of fusion welding process which makes use of electric arc for heat generation.
